sources.title: Satoru Iwata (Q316013) -- verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-10-24): English label 'Satoru Iwata', description 'Japanese video game programmer and businessman (1959-2015)', Korean label '이와타 사토루', born 6 December 1959, died 11 July 2015, citizenship Japan, P18 'Satoru Iwata GDC 2011 (cropped).jpg'. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

Tokyo Tech News, 'In memory of Satoru Iwata, Tokyo Tech alumnus and Nintendo president', 8 September 2015 (read in full): the university's summary of his path (School of Engineering entry 1978, part-time work at HAL Laboratory, full-time at HAL in 1982 after graduating, president of HAL in 1993, joined Nintendo in 2000, the DS and Wii developed under his leadership) with recollections from three Tokyo Tech professors -- classmate Tomohiko Uyematsu (honed his programming day and night on a Commodore PET and wrote programs faster and more accurately than anyone), lab senior Motoshi Saeki (graduation research on recognising handwritten mathematical expressions on a tablet, which he later saw as a prototype of the DS) and part-time co-worker Satoshi Matsuoka (HAL's early years). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE (with the Rolling Stone obituary). University tribute written after his death; admiring and retrospective, but by people who worked or studied with him; only the study and work behaviour is used, not the occasion.

Daniel Kreps, 'Satoru Iwata, President and CEO of Nintendo, Dead at 55', Rolling Stone, 13 July 2015 (read in full): HAL work on EarthBound, Kirby's Adventure and Balloon Fight; assisting Nintendo on Pokemon titles; joining Nintendo's corporate planning in 2000 and succeeding Hiroshi Yamauchi two years later after the GameCube; steering resources to the DS and Wii; the 3DS's underperformance after which he voluntarily halved his own salary to take responsibility; a consultant's remark that he 'created a whole culture'. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE (with the Tokyo Tech tribute). News obituary, mostly admiring but naming a failure; the cause-of-death and illness passages were not used.

Mark Brown, '4 times Satoru Iwata was a programming badass', Pocket Gamer, 13 July 2015 (read in full): Iwata as the only Nintendo president with a game-development background who kept programming as boss; offering the EarthBound team a clean rewrite instead of a two-year fix and delivering rewritten code after about a month (his own 2013 account); rebuilding Pokemon's battle system for Pokemon Stadium on the N64 from the Game Boy source in about a week, with Game Freak programmer Shigeki Morimoto quoted as 'What kind of company president is this!?'; about three weeks as acting head of debugging on Super Smash Bros. Melee at HAL in 2001 (his own account to 4Gamer); the writer flags the Pokemon Gold/Silver compression story as hard to source. Enthusiast-press tribute: part self-account, part independent colleague quote.

Shaun Nichols, 'Nintendo boss Satoru Iwata was MORE than a suit - he was a CODER', The Register, 13 July 2015 (read in full): programming credit he gave himself in a 1981 VIC-20 Galaxian game, HAL titles including EarthBound, Kirby and Pokemon; the Pokemon Stadium battle port in about a week from source alone with Morimoto's quote; president and representative director from 2002 and the first outside the Yamauchi family; the Wii for casual gamers and the DS; his role in the amiibo idea and the 2015 move toward smart-device software. Tech-press obituary; independent restatement of the Morimoto quote (so not a separate witness).

The Globe and Mail staff, 'Nintendo CEO remembered by gamers, industry' (13 July 2015, read in full): HAL president from 1993 after Kirby's Dream Land, Nintendo president from May 2002; the DS, Wii and amiibo; the writers' note that Nintendo struggled to adapt and resisted smartphone games until a May 2015 DeNA partnership; his 'gamer at heart' style, Iwata Asks interviews with developers, and his statement that he wanted to improve 'the position of video games in society' (from an Iwata Asks interview). News report with the subject's own quoted motive and a critical note on mobile; social-media tribute passages not used.

Toshi Nakamura, 'Smash Bros. Creator Remembers Satoru Iwata', Kotaku, 22 July 2015 (read in full): translation of Masahiro Sakurai's column in Weekly Famitsu -- Iwata had interviewed Sakurai when he applied to HAL; Sakurai's five descriptions (analysing and offering ideas rather than showing anger, quickly summarising what others meant, reading numerous management books and seeking advice, doing Iwata Asks and Nintendo Direct himself, emailing all employees and treating people as equals) and that his programmer years let him carry long projects to completion. Colleague's tribute through a translation, admiring; one voice; the passages on his health, a farewell dinner and Sakurai's own future are not used.

Eurogamer staff, 'GDC: Satoru Iwata keynote text commentary', 23 March 2006 (live text report of the 'Disrupting Development' keynote, read in full): Iwata's account of the Brain Training task force and the nine-person team given a short schedule, Dr Kawashima's one-hour meeting, requiring retailers in Japan to try the game, Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection built around Mario Kart DS and Animal Crossing and aimed at a friendly rather than 'aggressive' online atmosphere, the design of the Revolution controller (Miyamoto's one-handed idea, nunchuk added after Metroid developers objected), his critique of $50-60 games dependent on sequels, and the 'new continent' metaphor. Live report of his own speech: primary account of his strategy as he described it in 2006, filtered by a reporter's jokes; not used as proof of results.

NBC News, 'Game ender? Nintendo warns of third annual loss as Wii U sales flop', 17 January 2014 (read in full): Nintendo cutting its Wii U forecast by almost 70 percent to 2.8 million units and its 3DS forecast, a third annual loss, Iwata apologising to shareholders after a pledge to return to profit and saying there would be no major management shake-up, the contrast with the Wii success he architected in 2006, Nintendo's refusal to let its games run on rivals' machines or on mobile devices, and an asset-management chief saying the 'Wii U strategy' had failed. Business-news counter-voice on a contested stretch of his tenure.

Wikimedia Commons file pages 'Satoru Iwata GDC 2011 (cropped).jpg' and 'Satoru Iwata GDC 2011.jpg', plus the Flickr photo page of the Official GDC account (live check 2026-10-24) -- checked for the portrait: photograph from the Official GDC Flickr stream, 2 March 2011 (second day of GDC 2011), CC BY 2.0 with a human licence review on Commons.

mastery_orientation.rationale: [src_si_titech, src_si_pocketgamer, src_si_register, src_si_kotaku | 1978-2001 | university tribute + two press obituaries + colleague column] A Tokyo Tech classmate recalls him honing programming day and night on a Commodore PET and writing programs faster and more accurately than anyone; a Game Freak programmer says he rebuilt the Pokemon battle system on the N64 from source in about a week; Sakurai says his programmer years let him carry long projects through. Student-era and colleague accounts agree on deep, self-driven craft, while the EarthBound and Smash Melee stories are largely his own tellings. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): first-pass 74 / 0.62 lowered to 72 / 0.58 because two of the four headline stories (the EarthBound rewrite and the Melee debugging) rest on his own later accounts rather than a colleague's.

execution_speed.rationale: [src_si_titech, src_si_pocketgamer, src_si_register | 1978-2001 | university tribute + press obituaries] The classmate says he wrote programs faster and more accurately than anyone in his group; the Game Freak programmer's reaction to the week-long Pokemon port; his own account says he offered the EarthBound team a rewrite in half a year instead of two and produced rewritten code in about a month. Speed is documented by an independent classmate and programmer, with the project-level numbers resting on his own recollection, so a moderate confidence.

collaboration.rationale: [src_si_kotaku, src_si_pocketgamer, src_si_eurogamer, src_si_globe | 1990s-2015 | colleague column + press + keynote report] Sakurai says he treated everyone as equals, emailed all employees and did the Iwata Asks and Direct presentations himself; he stepped in on other teams' code at HAL while an executive; in 2006 he described the Revolution controller as shaped by Miyamoto's idea and Metroid developers' objections and his Iwata Asks interviews gave developers a public voice. One named colleague plus two reports of work with developers; the controller story is his own telling, so a moderate confidence.

opportunity_sensing.rationale: [src_si_rs, src_si_register, src_si_eurogamer, src_si_nbc | 2002-2014 | obituaries + keynote report + business news] Obituaries credit him with steering Nintendo toward the DS and the Wii (the Register calls the Wii the home console of choice for casual gamers; NBC calls him the architect of the 2006 Wii success), and in 2006 he described the Brain Training task force and a plan to reach non-players; against that the same business press documents the 2014 forecast collapse for the Wii U. A documented successful reading of a market opening, tempered by a later miss and by the reliance on his own account for the reasoning.

persuasiveness.rationale: [src_si_eurogamer, src_si_kotaku, src_si_globe | 2006-2015 | keynote report + colleague column + news report] He gave the 2006 GDC keynote in which he handed every attendee a copy of Brain Age and had game-industry figures play it on stage; Sakurai says he deliberately fronted Iwata Asks and Nintendo Direct to convey the company's message and could summarise others' points so anyone could understand. Public communication is documented, but the sources are a reporter's live blog and an admiring colleague, so a modest score and confidence.

adaptability.rationale: [src_si_globe, src_si_nbc, src_si_rs | 2002-2015 | news reports + obituary] The Globe and Mail says Nintendo resisted smartphone games and preferred its own hardware until a May 2015 DeNA partnership; NBC reports the 2014 loss, his apology and a refusal to put games on rival machines, while Rolling Stone notes the DS and Wii shift after the GameCube. A real change of direction in 2015 after a long hold-out, hence a middling score with dual-edged impact; the reasons are not documented in these sources.

impact_motivation.rationale: [src_si_globe, src_si_kotaku | 2000s-2015 | news report quoting an Iwata Asks interview + colleague column] He is quoted as saying that if non-players are not brought to understand games their position in society will not improve; Sakurai says he chose to front communication such as Iwata Asks despite the risk of criticism. The motive is mostly his own statement, supported by one colleague's description of behaviour, so confidence is capped low.

provenance.notes: PREFLIGHT: QID VERIFIED LIVE: Wikidata wbgetentities (2026-10-24) for Q316013 returned en label 'Satoru Iwata', description 'Japanese video game programmer and businessman (1959-2015)', ko label '이와타 사토루', born 1959-12-06, died 2015-07-11, citizenship Japan, P18 'Satoru Iwata GDC 2011 (cropped).jpg'. SLUG/QID CHECK: no data-pipeline candidate or src file for slug satoru-iwata or QID Q316013. REGION: east_asia (Japan). VOCABULARY: occupations executive, engineer (no programmer/game-developer label exists); fields business, technology; tags product_leader, innovator; archetypes technical_innovator, organizational_leader are existing labelled ids with EN and KO labels. ZERO POLITICS: nothing political. DECEASED SUBJECT: no inference from his illness, surgery, death or the funeral; all bile-duct, medical, cause-of-death and fan-tribute passages were excluded and tributes are used only for descriptions of his work conduct. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCES: Tokyo Tech News alumni tribute (https://www.titech.ac.jp/english/news/2015/032130) and the Rolling Stone obituary (https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/news/satoru-iwata-president-and-ceo-of-nintendo-dead-at-55-20150713); both read in full via local text extraction. READ (9 cited non-Wikidata sources): Tokyo Tech, Rolling Stone, Pocket Gamer, The Register, The Globe and Mail, Kotaku (Sakurai column), Eurogamer GDC 2006 live text, NBC News 2014, plus the Commons/Flickr page for the portrait. Not opened or blocked: the New York Times obituary (403), Guardian (404), Bloomberg Wii U article (blocked), Tokyo Weekender (522), the Iwata Asks interviews themselves, the Itoi EarthBound account and Time 2015 interview (known only through other writers), the GDC Vault video (maintenance page). The Hacker News/Itoi claim that Iwata saved EarthBound was seen only as a search snippet and is not carded. PERSPECTIVES: university colleagues and classmates (Tokyo Tech), a game-industry peer (Morimoto via Pocket Gamer and the Register; Sakurai via Kotaku), news obituaries (Rolling Stone, Register, Globe), his own talks and interviews (Eurogamer 2006; quoted Iwata Asks and 4Gamer remarks in Pocket Gamer and the Globe), and business news (NBC 2014). The Pocket Gamer and Register pieces share the Morimoto quote, so they are one witness. COUNTER-VOICES: NBC on the failed Wii U strategy and the 2014 loss, the Globe on resisting mobile games, Rolling Stone on the 3DS underperformance and the halved salary. Self-only evidence: the EarthBound rewrite, the Melee debugging and his motive statement are his own accounts and are never sole support. SELF-CALIBRATION: reviewed mastery_orientation (lowered, see row), execution_speed (kept: the classmate and the Game Freak programmer are independent of his own stories) and impact_motivation (kept at 58 / 0.40, already capped for self-report). The salary cut is not scored as a trait row. PORTRAIT: Official GDC Flickr CC BY 2.0 photograph, see portrait.source.
